_:
x2 — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 runes on Cloudflare Workers, Qdrant for storage, pnpm only, never npm or npx.

REPO RULES: runes only, never `export let`. snake_case for vars and functions. single-letter payload keys. all UI text lowercase. Tailwind utilities only — no inline `style=`, no `<style>` blocks, use the tokens in src/app.css. No comments except a non-obvious WHY. Never start the dev server.

COMMANDS: tests are `pnpm test` (vitest run). Types are `bash plan/check_budget.sh` — svelte-check carries 14 known pre-existing errors and exits non-zero even on a clean tree, so NEVER gate on `pnpm check` itself. eslint also carries ~99 pre-existing errors repo-wide (20+ in ws/, which this work never touches), so never gate on `pnpm lint` either; prettier must be clean.

THE PRODUCT RULE THIS BATCH ENCODES: watching is free, talking is what needs an account. Rooms, profiles, room search and people search are all readable signed out. Exactly two things are held back. A user's phone number (`w`) is what an account buys, because it is a direct line to a person and an open profile is a page Google keeps forever. Interests (`i`) are shown to nobody ever, because people must be able to write down everything they are into, including what they would not want known, and still be matched on it.

TRAP THAT DRIVES SEVERAL STEPS: whatever a `+page.server.ts` load returns is serialised into the page HTML. A field the component does not render is still in view-source. Privacy is enforced in the loader, never in the markup.

ROUTES, after the previous commit: /@username is a profile, /~handle is a room, /find is people search, /rooms browses rooms, /chats and /chat/<uid> are threads. /app/*, /rooms/<id> and /groups/<rest> are 308 shims to the new homes.

ALREADY CHANGED AND UNCOMMITTED WHEN THIS PLAN WAS WRITTEN — do not redo any of it: src/routes/+layout.svelte (the `fit` regex, which had kept naming the old /app routes and left the composer floating mid-page); src/routes/+layout.server.ts (the signed-out open list); src/lib/server/group.ts (`is_member` now trusts the stored `mb` before asking the hub, which is what unbroke posting in a room created while the hub was down); src/routes/~[handle]/+page.server.ts (messages load for everyone); src/routes/api/groups/+server.ts and src/routes/api/search/+server.ts (GET no longer 401s); src/routes/@[username]/+page.server.ts (phone gate); src/routes/@[username]/+page.svelte (the interests block is gone from the markup).

open_gates.s:
OUTCOME: signed-out visitors can reach every open page and both searches, and the suite is green again.

1. Five tests still assert the old gated behaviour and must now assert the open behaviour instead: `redirects a logged-out visitor from /rooms to /login` in src/routes/__tests__/layout.server.test.ts; `401s when signed out` in src/routes/@[username]/__tests__/page.server.test.ts; `serves an anonymous visitor the room and names but no message history` in src/routes/~[handle]/__tests__/page.server.test.ts (an anonymous visitor now DOES get the history); `401s when signed out` in src/routes/api/groups/__tests__/server.test.ts (only the `mine=1` branch still 401s); `401s when not logged in` in src/routes/api/search/__tests__/server.test.ts.
2. Two type errors came in with the open-access edits. src/routes/api/groups/+server.ts line 13: `locals.user` is possibly null in the `mine` branch. src/routes/api/search/+server.ts line 45: `locals.device_id` is `string | undefined`. hooks.server.ts sets device_id on every single request, so narrow it at the call site — do not loosen `guard`'s signature.
3. src/routes/~[handle]/__tests__/page.server.test.ts builds its event with `params: { id: 'g1' }`, but the route reads `params.handle`. It passes only because get_group is mocked. Correct the param name while you are in the file.
4. The 308 shims at /rooms/<id> and /groups/<rest> are still behind the signed-out login redirect, so an old room link shared with a stranger lands on /login instead of the room. Add both prefixes to the open list in src/routes/+layout.server.ts.

FENCE: interests and the icons belong to later steps.
open_gates.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test

profile_privacy.s:
OUTCOME: the profile loader hands out only what a reader is allowed to have, proved by a staged test.

1. Copy the staged test, byte for byte, and never edit it:
   cp 'plan/tests/src/routes/@[username]/__tests__/privacy.test.ts.txt' 'src/routes/@[username]/__tests__/privacy.test.ts'
2. It will fail on interests. src/routes/@[username]/+page.server.ts must strip `i` from the user payload it returns, for every reader including the signed-in one. Removing the markup block was not enough — see the serialisation trap in the preamble.
3. The phone gate in that same loader is already written and the staged test locks it. Leave it alone unless the test says otherwise.

DECIDED: strip in the loader by rebuilding the returned object, so a new sensitive field added to User later is opt-in rather than leaked by default.
profile_privacy.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && test -f 'src/routes/@[username]/__tests__/privacy.test.ts' && bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test

interests_toggle_gone.s:
OUTCOME: nothing anywhere offers to publish interests, and the `si` field is gone end to end.

1. src/routes/profile/+page.svelte: remove the `Checkbox` bound to `showInterests`, the `showInterests` `$state`, and `show_interests` from the save body. In its place put one short lowercase line under the interests field saying interests are private and used only for matching.
2. src/lib/server/profile.ts: drop `show_interests` from the input type and the `si` write.
3. src/routes/api/profile/+server.ts: drop `show_interests` from the body type and from the save_profile call.
4. src/lib/types.ts: drop `si?: boolean` from the User type. Old points keep the key in Qdrant and nothing reads it, so there is no migration.
5. src/lib/server/__tests__/profile.test.ts: the whole `describe('show_interests flag')` block tests behaviour that no longer exists. Delete the block.

FENCE: leave the interests input itself, and leave `i` on the User type. Interests are still collected and still drive matching.
interests_toggle_gone.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && ! grep -rq 'show_interests' src/ && ! grep -rq 'u\.si' src/ && bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test

homepage_doors.s:
OUTCOME: the homepage is the voice match plus two doors, and carries no server data of its own.

WHY, so you do not rebuild it: a stranger landing here has no query in mind, so a search box asks a question they cannot answer yet. Two labelled doors teach what the place holds. /rooms and /find already have the real search with filters, and a mini-search here would only be a worse copy.

1. Delete src/routes/+page.server.ts and src/routes/__tests__/page.server.test.ts. The page needs nothing but `user`, which the root layout already provides.
2. src/routes/+page.svelte: remove the search input, both result lists, `q`, `people`, `load_people`, `run_search`, the `load_people` call inside onMount, and the `goto` and `Search` imports once they are unused.
3. In their place, under the start button, put two doors — rooms first, then people. Each is a link with a label and one lowercase line of copy. The rooms line must say that a room reads without an account, because that is the strongest thing this page can offer a stranger. No counts and no result previews: the app is new and '1 room open' reads worse than saying nothing.
4. src/routes/__tests__/page.svelte.test.ts renders with `data: { user, q, rooms }`. Drop `q` and `rooms`, and replace the two room-result assertions with assertions for the two doors.
homepage_doors.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && test ! -f src/routes/+page.server.ts && test ! -f src/routes/__tests__/page.server.test.ts && grep -q 'href="/rooms"' src/routes/+page.svelte && grep -q 'href="/find"' src/routes/+page.svelte && bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test

heart_icons.s:
OUTCOME: every PNG in static/icons is the x2 heart instead of the black diagonal placeholder that is there now.

DECIDED, do not redesign: the heart geometry is exactly the three shapes in static/logo.svg — a square turned 45 degrees with a circle on each upper edge. Fill #d98b5f on a solid #0b0b0c field, which is what the header shows and what the manifest already names as theme_color and background_color.

1. Sizes must not change, because src/lib/__tests__/pwa-assets.test.ts asserts each one against static/manifest.webmanifest: icon-192 192, icon-512 512, icon-192-maskable 192, icon-512-maskable 512, badge-96 96, apple-touch-icon 180.
2. The two maskable files get the heart scaled to about 60 percent and centred, because Android crops a maskable icon to a circle and anything in the corners is lost.
3. badge-96.png is declared `purpose: monochrome`, so it is a solid #000000 heart on transparent. The OS recolours a silhouette and a two-tone badge comes out wrong.
4. inkscape is installed and is the converter. Write the intermediate SVGs to a scratch directory, never into static/.
5. Leave the two screenshot PNGs alone.
heart_icons.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && test "$(sha256sum -c plan/icons.before.sha 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': OK')" -eq 0 && bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test

ship.s:
OUTCOME: the whole batch is one commit on master and pushed.

1. Run `pnpm format`, then confirm `pnpm exec prettier --check .` is clean.
2. Stage with `git add -A ':!.log' ':!.dev-logs'` — those two are live dev-server output and never belong in a commit.
3. One commit, Conventional Commits with a body: the subject is imperative, under 50 characters, lowercase after the colon, no trailing period. The body covers open access, the two privacy holdbacks, the homepage doors, and the icons, at the level of intent rather than file by file.
4. Push. A failed push is fine, the commit is what matters.
5. Commit the archived plan that this step's mark moves into wip-plans/.
ship.t: bash plan/check_budget.sh && pnpm test && pnpm exec prettier --check . && test -z "$(git status --porcelain src/ static/)"
